appraisal_events.evidence: je sentais qu'il n'y aurait plus de paix pour moi avant que je l'eusse revue... je passais et repassais dans le couloir, espérant qu'elle sortirait et m'appellerait; je restais immobile devant sa porte... longtemps après, glacé, je revenais me mettre sous mes couvertures et pleurais tout le reste de la nuit.
appraisal_events.explanation: Unreconciled after the evening's tension, the narrator relives his childhood anguish over his mother's goodnight kiss, reduced to pacing the corridor, lingering outside Albertine's dark door, and weeping alone all night.

appraisal_events.evidence: je n'étais pas loin de croire Françoise supérieure à Bergotte et à Elstir parce qu'elle m'avait dit, à Balbec: « Cette fille-là ne vous causera que du chagrin. »
appraisal_events.explanation: In his anxious preoccupation with Albertine, the narrator half-seriously ranks Françoise's homely prophecy above the judgment of Bergotte and Elstir, an elevation he himself flags as a biased 'intellectual egoism.'

status_effects.explanation: The narrator regresses into a childlike state of anxious dependency, reduced to a humiliating, fruitless vigil outside Albertine's door and left weeping alone through the night.
Albertine unknowingly holds the emotional advantage as the withheld object of the narrator's desperate need, retiring indifferent to his silent vigil outside her door.
The narrator credits Françoise with a superior judgment to Bergotte and Elstir on the strength of one lucky remark, a lightly ironized but locally real elevation.
